question: Will United Russia (ER) gain the most seats in the next Russian parliamentary election?
resolution_criteria:
Parliamentary elections are to be scheduled to be held in Russia in September 2026.

This market will resolve according to the political party that gains the greatest number of seats in the next Russian State Duma election, compared to before the election.

If the results are not known definitively by September 30, 2027, 11:59 PM ET, this market will resolve to "Other".

In the event of a tie between multiple parties for the most seats gained, this market will resolve in favor of the party that received a greater number of valid votes. In the event that results in a tie, this market will resolve in favor of the party whose listed abbreviation appears first in alphabetical order.

This market's resolution will be based solely on the number of seats gained by the named party in the State Duma of the Federal Assembly of the Russian Federation.

This market will resolve based on the results of this election, as indicated by a consensus of credible reporting. If there is ambiguity, this market will resolve based solely on the official results reported by Russian government sources such as the Central Election Commission of the Russian Federation.
research:
I could only use sources dated on or before 2026-09-11. Several search results were dated after that and I left them out. Every direct page fetch was refused by the proxy, so the figures below come from search-result summaries and should be checked.

The question is about seats **gained**, meaning the change from each party's pre-election seat count. It is not about total seats.

## 1. Resolution source
- The criteria give no URL. The deciding source is a consensus of credible reporting, with the Central Election Commission (CEC) as the fallback. I could not get any primary CEC page from before the cutoff.
- 2021-09-24: Baseline from the last election (CEC, via TASS and Interfax): United Russia 324, CPRF 57, A Just Russia 27, LDPR 21, New People 13, Rodina / Civic Platform / Party of Growth 1 each, independents 5. [TASS](https://tass.com/politics/1343197/amp), [Interfax](https://interfax.com/newsroom/top-stories/72754/)
- After 2021: Wikipedia says two deputies joined United Russia, two joined New People and one joined A Just Russia after the election. Other changes from vacancies and resignations followed. I could not confirm the exact faction sizes just before the 2026 vote; one figure I saw put United Russia at about 310, but I could not trace it to a pre-cutoff source. This matters, because "gain" is likely measured against the outgoing seat count, which could be 2021 results or the faction sizes on the eve of the election. [8th State Duma, Wikipedia](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/8th_State_Duma)

## 2. Current status
- As of 2026-09-11 nothing is settled. Voting is scheduled for September 18-20, 2026. The question turns on whether United Russia's net seat change (new total minus pre-election total) is larger than any other party's. The bar is fairly high: winning the most seats is not enough. United Russia must keep at least its starting number and out-gain the CPRF, New People and the others. [Moscow Times](https://www.themoscowtimes.com/2026/07/02/russia-is-gearing-up-for-nationwide-elections-this-is-what-you-need-to-know-a93142)

## 3. Recent news (newest first)
- 2026-08-07: A VTsIOM survey of July data put United Russia at 34% of all respondents, CPRF at 11% and New People at 10%. It said 56% of Russians had already decided how to vote. [bne IntelliNews](https://www.intellinews.com/more-than-half-of-russians-have-already-decided-how-they-ll-vote-in-duma-election-poll-459788/)
- 2026-07-24: FOM had United Russia down 3 points to 33%, its lowest since February 2022. VTsIOM had it down 2.6 points to 32.7%. The Anti-Corruption Foundation (FBK) put it at 16%. [Novaya Gazeta Europe](https://novayagazeta.eu/amp/en/articles/2026/07/24/ruling-united-russia-party-s-approval-rating-hits-lowest-level-since-start-of-full-scale-war-en-news)
- Mid-2026: VTsIOM changed its methodology to combine phone and door-to-door surveys after Putin's ratings fell. [Mezha](https://mezha.net/eng/bukvy/6822b18a_russian_state_pollster/)
- 2026-07-02: The Moscow Times called United Russia the expected dominant party. Half the seats are elected by party list and half in single-member districts, where United Russia usually takes most seats. [Moscow Times](https://www.themoscowtimes.com/2026/07/02/russia-is-gearing-up-for-nationwide-elections-this-is-what-you-need-to-know-a93142)
- The Council on Foreign Relations called United Russia keeping its majority "a good bet". I could not find a seat projection. [Wikipedia election page](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2026_Russian_legislative_election)
- Free Russia think tank pre-election monitoring tracks party ratings. [4freerussia](https://thinktank.4freerussia.org/politics/monitoring-the-pre-election-situation-in-russia-fourth-issue)

## 4. Base rates
- United Russia seat totals: 2007: 315. 2011: 238 (−77). 2016: 343 (+105). 2021: 324 (−19). It gained seats in 2 of the last 4 elections. In 2011 and 2021 other parties (CPRF, A Just Russia) gained the most. Swings between elections are large, often tens of seats.
- In 2021 United Russia got 49.82% of the list vote while its pre-election polls showed about 27-30%. Official results have regularly come in far above state-pollster ratings.
- The mixed system is decisive. In 2016 and 2021, United Russia won about 200 or more of the 225 district seats. Its district haul matters more than its list share.
- With United Russia starting below its 2021 total because of attrition (if the eve-of-election count is the baseline), even a flat result would count as a gain.

## 5. Other forecasts
- Polymarket has a market titled "Will United Russia (ER) gain the most seats…" (this question). I could not read its price because the fetch failed. [SimpleFunctions mirror](https://simplefunctions.dev/markets/0x502a94e5c525766d5ee7f16c6568131ba1b2cbadb69c703af05a6ef00336ed64), [Lines](https://www.lines.com/prediction-markets/elections/which-party-will-gain-most-seats-in-russian-parliamentary-election), [Octagon](https://www.octagonai.co/markets/politics/politics/which-party-will-gain-most-seats-in-russian-parliamentary-election/)
- The separate "win the most seats" market was reported at about 95% in July 2026, per an aggregator. That is a different question from this one. [SimpleFunctions](https://simplefunctions.dev/markets/0x94ffc785f73c9d70c0c9550b2412842d025d20d02f9e9e20a18cc4598944cbc5)
- The "United Russia wins every region" market was at about 69% in August 2026. [Orrery](https://orrery.me/markets/russia-elections-united-russia-wins-every-region)
- An April 2026 piece described the United Russia market sliding from 80¢ to 66¢. It was internally inconsistent (it also cites 58%). [CryptoSlate](https://cryptoslate.com/?p=547262)
- I found no Kalshi or Manifold market.

## 6. Upcoming events before resolution
- 2026-09-18 to 09-20: Voting, including multi-day and online voting.
- About 09-21: Preliminary CEC results.
- About a week after the vote: Final CEC seat distribution. Gains will depend on the pre-election baseline used, and on whether parties near the 5% threshold (A Just Russia, New People) get in.
- The 8th Duma's term ends 2026-09-30.

**Main uncertainty:** whether "gain" is measured against 2021 results (324) or against faction sizes on the eve of the election (lower, figure unconfirmed).

forecasts.reasoning:
eline is likely below 324, possibly about 310, because of vacancies and departures (8th Duma, Wikipedia; unconfirmed figure).
  - Official results ran about 20 points above state polls in 2021 (49.8% versus about 28%).
  - The Moscow Times (2026-07-02) and CFR both expect United Russia dominance.
  - 56% of voters had already decided (VTsIOM, 2026-08-07), which favours a mobilised administrative vote.
- For No:
  - FOM and VTsIOM ratings hit their lowest since February 2022: 33% and 32.7% (2026-07-24).
  - LDPR and New People were polling around 10%, up from their 2021 shares. They could gain 10-20 seats each from small bases.
  - If the Kremlin chooses to spread seats to "systemic" parties, United Russia could end flat or slightly down.

**(e) Scenarios.**
- No: The Kremlin settles for a comfortable but smaller majority of about 300-315. New People rises from about 15 to about 30, LDPR from about 22 to about 40, and LDPR is the top gainer.
- Yes: United Russia takes about 55% of the list vote plus about 200 districts, reaching about 335. That is a gain of 10-25 seats over its pre-election count, beating the smaller parties' gains.

**(f) Adjustment.** I start near 50% from the base rate and move toward the market anchor of about 60%. The likely below-324 baseline and the Kremlin's preference for a strong showing push up. Weak polls and possible growth for LDPR and New People push down. Uncertainty over which baseline is used keeps me from going much higher.

Probability: 60%

forecasts_with_market.reasoning:
nt a constitutional majority in wartime, and district seats are reliably captured.
  - The Moscow Times (2026-07-02) and CFR both expect United Russia to dominate.
- **For No:**
  - FOM had United Russia at 33% and VTsIOM at 32.7% on 2026-07-24, the lowest since February 2022.
  - In 2021 United Russia lost 19 seats despite heavy administrative control, and the CPRF gained the most.
  - New People (10%) could clear the threshold more comfortably and gain seats.

(e) **Scenarios.**
- **No:** The Kremlin tolerates a slightly lower United Russia list share to manage discontent and settles around 300-315 seats. Measured against 324, that is a loss. The CPRF or New People each gain 5-15 seats and resolution is based on 2021 totals.
- **Yes:** United Russia is again officially reported near 50% of the list vote and takes about 200 or more districts, for 320-335 seats. That is a gain over the depleted eve-of-election faction while the CPRF stays flat or loses. Alternatively, resolution effectively treats "gain" as "win."

(f) **From base rate to final probability.** I start from a structural prior of about 60%. The liquid market on the identical question sits at 78%. It likely prices in both the baseline ambiguity and the managed-election dynamics. I have no specific evidence the market has missed, apart from the soft polling, which it already reflects. I therefore anchor close to the market and shade slightly down for the baseline ambiguity and the 2021 precedent.

Probability: 75%
